opps.title: 2 accounts stopped ordering — $307 of commission gone quiet
opps.body: Each of these bought from you last year and has ordered nothing at all in 2026. A lost account is the most expensive kind of decline: there is no brand mix to fix and nothing replaces it automatically — the whole relationship has stopped. The largest, Kilroy's (A), was worth 269 cases last year on its own. These are the calls with the shortest path back to commission, because the account already knows you.

opps.title: 2 accounts holding all year but soft this month — 1,469 cases behind
opps.body: Year to date each of these is fine, so the relationship is not the problem — but month to date they are all well behind where they were last August. That is the pattern that becomes a bad quarter if nobody catches it, and it is the cheapest kind to fix: the account is still buying, it just has not placed its usual order yet. Together they are 1,469 cases and about $1,469 of commission behind last August's pace, with days left in the month to close it.

opps.body: Still ordering, but 900 cases lighter than last year (16%). It is your #16 account and 2.2% of your commission, so the slide is worth about $900 in modeled commission. The drop is concentrated in Lite (-156 cases), Twisted Tea (-123 cases) — a mix problem you can work on the next visit, not a lost account.
